The VIX closed at 35.9 on Friday’s monthly options expiration, its highest on an expiration day since April 2020.

Since 1990, there have been 30 expirations with the VIX at 30 or higher. What the S&P 500 did next (vs. all days):

▪ First week: a coin flip, higher about half the time.
▪ One month: median +4.4%, higher 77% of the time (all days +1.2%, 64%).
▪ Six months: median +17.4%, higher in 28 of 30 (all days +5.7%, 75%).
▪ The catch: the median worst close within three months was −4.9%, and in September 2008 the index fell 21.5% in a month.

Counting only the first expiration in each run (12 cases), the S&P 500 was higher six months later 11 of 12 times.

Of course, market returns exhibit "fat tails," meaning extreme moves occur more frequently than a normal distribution would predict.

Volatility returns when markets least expect it.

This is basic stuff, but I feel like many emerging teams need a reminder.

Your paid ads are burning money if you:

1. Judge performance by ROAS alone.
2. Ignore a declining CTR when conversions remain stable.
3. Don’t investigate why a high CTR leads to fewer conversions.
4. Overlook rising CPMs when CTR stays flat.
5. Keep running ads as CTR and conversion rates decline.
6. Rarely test new creative concepts.
7. Ignore ad frequency and creative fatigue.
8. Make decisions based on a single bad day.
9. Don’t compare 7-day vs. 30-day performance trends.
10. Wait for ROAS to drop before investigating performance issues.

PS: In many cases, paid ads aren’t efficient at all.

So check your acquisition benchmarks against average customer acquisition costs by channel.

FYI: Paid ads are the most-used channel for teams at $50M+ ARR – because they CAN afford it.

A very sobering practice.

We have now been dragged back into that “what if there is a bug and it goes to zero” phase. Only time will overcome this again, like it did in the early part of Bitcoin’s lifecycle. 

I roughly think 2027 is 2019 for this reason, and who knows maybe another scare again in 2028, before new highs late 28/29. 

If quantum isn’t properly addressed in a convincing way next year then odds are much higher of this being Bitcoin’s first failed cycle.

“Open source needs to be allowed and frankly encouraged to proliferate because the absence of that means that you're going to have tyrannical groups, ultimately, they become tyrannical.

They don't intend to be tyrannical, but every group that has the power to control what people see, what they're allowed to do, what they're allowed to access, how they're allowed to use things, what those specific weights are on ‘facts of history,’ on ‘proven science,’ on ‘the truth.’

That is where people become tyrannical because they have an opinion where they think they're right, and if they have the power, they will act on that opinion, and it will ultimately give them tyrannical force over a broader population.

I've been playing with Gemini 4 Neon for 5 straight days. Google gave me early access and sponsored today's episode.

10 insights using Gemini 4 Neon (for people who want to make cool things with AI):

1. Type /swarm and give it a researcher, a designer and a couple of engineers. I'd point it at a small directory or app for a niche and let it run overnight. 

2. The physics are so good that I'd mock up a hardware product or a little game with it before spending a dollar on either.

3. I gave it my company's messy invoices and asked for a financial model. Now I go back and forth with it like I've got a CFO on call.

4. Paste in a local business's website and it'll read the whole thing and build them something useful, like a calculator or a new homepage. Interesting cash flow idea there.

5. Make a mini game or a 3D customizer for your product and put an email box in front of it. It's way more fun than a PDF, and people share them.

6. Drop every customer call from last quarter into AI Studio and ask it what you promised and never shipped. It can hold about a million tokens at once, and it stays sharp the whole way through.

9. Set the thinking to high and build in Antigravity, even though the app still has some catching up to do. The same model scored three times higher there on a coding test.

10. It's a really good writer once you tell it to drop the em dashes. It's also brief, so ask for more when you want more.

TLDR; it's a REALLY good money for WAY cheaper than we're used to. So, you can be way more loose on the types of projects you build and agents you have running.
